Training monotony and strain

Source: R/descriptors.R
monotony_strain.Rd

Computes Foster's (1998) training monotony and strain for every day, over a rolling window of window days (7 by default), within each athlete (MODELS.md, M-12).

Usage

monotony_strain(x, window = 7, same_day_load = c("include", "exclude"))

Arguments

x

A daily_load object, from as_daily_load(). It is checked first; an object changed after it was built (for example by subsetting) must be rebuilt with as_daily_load().

window

Length of the window in days, a single whole number >= 2.

same_day_load

Whether the window ends on the current day ("include", the default) or on the previous day ("exclude").

Value

A data frame with one row per row of x, in the same order, and the columns athlete, date, load, window_load, mean_load, sd_load, monotony and strain. The attributes window and same_day_load record the arguments used.

Formula

For the loads of the window, $$\mathrm{monotony} = \frac{\mathrm{mean\ load}}{\mathrm{SD\ of\ the\ loads}}, \qquad \mathrm{strain} = \mathrm{window\ load} \times \mathrm{monotony},$$ where the window load is the sum of the loads and the SD is the sample standard deviation (divisor \(k - 1\)). Foster (1998) defines them over a week; the package uses a rolling window computed every day (D-022). The window is the one of rolling_load() (MODELS.md, M-11).

Timing option and default

With same_day_load = "include" (the default) the window ends on the current day; with "exclude" it ends on the previous day. The default differs from the impulse-response models, whose default is "exclude" (DECISIONS.md, D-021 and D-012).

Missing, rest and equal days

  • A day with a missing load makes every window that contains it NA in every result column (D-016). Windows that do not fit in the series are NA: there are no partial windows.

  • Rest days count as load 0. Foster (1998) does not say how rest days are treated; the result depends on this choice.

  • When all loads of the window are equal (for example seven rest days), sd_load is 0 and monotony and strain are NA (D-022). Equality is tested on the loads themselves, not on the computed standard deviation.

Monotony divides by a standard deviation, so it is unstable when the days of the window are similar. The article "Monotony and strain" on the package website discusses its limitations.

Acute

chronic workload ratio: Ratios of rolling loads and EWMA-based loads are not provided here: see the ACWR package (DECISIONS.md, D-019).

References

Foster C (1998). Monitoring training in athletes with reference to overtraining syndrome. Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise, 30(7), 1164-1168.

See also

rolling_load(), srpe_load(), as_daily_load().

Examples

# The week of Foster (1998), Table 1
week <- data.frame(
  date = as.Date("2026-01-04") + 0:6,
  load = srpe_load(rpe = c(5, 7, 2, 6, 7, 2, 7),
                   duration = c(180, 120, 20, 90, 75, 20, 120))
)
x <- as_daily_load(week, date = "date", load = "load")
monotony_strain(x)
#>   athlete       date load window_load mean_load  sd_load monotony   strain
#> 1       1 2026-01-04  900          NA        NA       NA       NA       NA
#> 2       1 2026-01-05  840          NA        NA       NA       NA       NA
#> 3       1 2026-01-06   40          NA        NA       NA       NA       NA
#> 4       1 2026-01-07  540          NA        NA       NA       NA       NA
#> 5       1 2026-01-08  525          NA        NA       NA       NA       NA
#> 6       1 2026-01-09   40          NA        NA       NA       NA       NA
#> 7       1 2026-01-10  840        3725  532.1429 367.2857 1.448853 5396.976
